title: POC workshop accelerator weekplan and issue handoff
content:
Context and goal:

This doc captures the 4-week accelerated POC plan that we ran with Acme Retail (placeholder), workshop notes from the Day 0 kickoff, an issue handoff checklist for SRE/Platform, and a short decision & risk register. The goal for the POC: validate a production-grade integration of Redwood Dedicated endpoints for customer search re-ranking and answer generation with a target 99th percentile latency < 220 ms and cost <= $/1000 tokens target set by customer (see acceptance criteria). This is an operational-focused POC: prove routing/fallbacks, autoscale behavior, and prompt-level regression monitoring.

High-level sprint plan (4-week accelerated):

Week 0 (pre-kickoff, 3 business days)
- Deliverables: access configured (VPC peering request ticket), API key provisioned for dedicated test cluster, sample data schema shared.
- Owners: SE (Aisha) to confirm access; Platform (Devon) to provision sandbox capacity; Customer IAM (Acme) to approve peering.
- Risks: networking approvals may take >3 days — mitigation: request temporary VPN tunnel.

Week 1 (Kickoff & integration)
- Day 1: 2h Kickoff workshop agenda: intro & goals (15m), infra overview (20m), prompt/evaller walkthrough (30m), integration checklist (30m), open Q&A (25m). Notes: customer wanted explicit routing by region for GDPR traffic.
- Tasks: embed SDK into customer staging search pipeline (Riley), map tokenization expectations for their 512-token limit (Marco), baseline CPU/GPU memory using sample queries (Devon).
- Acceptance to proceed: successful end-to-end request/response with sample dataset and tracing visible in Console for 10 requests.

Week 2 (Stress & failover testing)
- Tasks: generate 1k concurrent requests at expected QPS and observe batching behavior; inject node failure to validate fallback to smaller model; measure tail latency with KV caching toggled on/off (Samira).
- Deliverables: stress test report (latency distribution, p99/p95), fallback-playbook log entries, recommended batching config.

Week 3 (Quality & cost tuning)
- Tasks: run eval harness on 200 seeded prompts, compare generation quality between model variants; experiment with 4-bit quantized model, measure quality delta and cost savings; apply Redwood Optimize recommendations and re-run 100 hotpath queries.
- Deliverables: quality regression summary, cost projection spreadsheet, suggested rollout policy for canary.

Week 4 (Handover & closeout)
- Tasks: prepare runbook and SLOs, finalize monitoring alerts, run smoke tests from customer infra, present results in final review workshop.
- Deliverables: handoff checklist completed, production readiness signoff (if passed), retention of test logs for 30 days.

Daily/Weekly cadences:
- Weekly sync (Mon 11:00 PT) — review blockers and action items (SE lead + customer PM + Platform engineer).
- Ad-hoc: Slack thread for immediate triage (solutions-poc channel).

Kickoff workshop notes (Day 1 detailed):
- Attendees: Aisha (SE), Marco (Applied ML), Riley (DX), Devon (Platform), Sam from Acme (PM), Li Wei (Acme infra), Tara (Acme data).
- Key decisions made: use dedicated sandbox cluster in us-west-2 for low-latency path; GDPR-sensitive traffic will route to eu-central-1 variant; KV cache to be enabled for re-ranking hot keys.
- Open questions: customer encryption-at-rest policy requires KMS integration — RESOLVE before Week 2. Owner: Devon.
- Immediate actions: create VPC peering ticket (Acme -> Action ID: JIRA-4320), create temporary API key and share via Secrets Manager (Aisha).

Integration checklist (must pass before Week 2):
- VPC peering / network test completed.
- Dedicated API key provisioned and tested from customer staging.
- SDK integrated and basic schema mapping done (tokens estimates validated).
- Tracing present in Redwood Console with correlationIDs.
- Test dataset (100 queries) executed end-to-end and results stored.

Acceptance criteria (explicit):
- Functional: re-ranking endpoint returns results consistent with baseline within NDCG delta <= 0.05 on seeded eval set.
- Performance: p95 latency < 150 ms, p99 latency < 220 ms under expected QPS (as measured in stress test).
- Reliability: automatic fallback to smaller model on node failure within 8 seconds, no dropped requests.
- Observability: per-route token and latency breakdown visible in Console; alert fires when p99 > 300 ms for 5m.
- Security: data path uses customer KMS for keys in dedicated environment.

Decision log (quick):
- D1 (2025-02-10): Sandbox region = us-west-2 for primary dev; eu-central-1 reserved for GDPR traffic routing. Owners: Aisha / Devon.
- D2 (2025-02-11): Use prefixed KV caching for session keys up to 2k unique keys. Owner: Marco.
- D3 (2025-02-14): Canary rollout window = 24h with 10% traffic, auto-rollback threshold p99+latency 2x baseline. Owner: Riley.

Risk register (top items and mitigations):
- R1: Networking delay - mitigation: temporary VPN and escalate to account manager for peering priority. Owner: Aisha.
- R2: KMS integration complexity - mitigation: use customer-managed KMS + short-lived test keys and create ticket for compliance review. Owner: Devon.
- R3: Quality regression after quantization - mitigation: keep unquantized variant available for fallback and include quality checks in CI eval. Owner: Marco.
- R4: Burst pricing spike - mitigation: set rate limits and a cost alert in Console with a hard cap for sandbox. Owner: Riley.

Issue handoff checklist for SRE/Platform (end of Week 2):
- Confirm dedicated cluster node types and instance counts in infra ticket.
- Export and attach stress test load generator configs to playbook.
- Provide runbook for node replacement and step-by-step fallback activation.
- Confirm retention policy for logs and traces (30 days) and who has access.
- Lease the canary model variant and provide model version tags.

Postmortem / retrospective prompts (for end of POC):
- What surprised us in latency under production-shaped load?
- Which prompts caused unexpected token spikes?
- Did caching behavior match expectations?
- Where can we reduce developer friction in onboarding?

Artifacts to deliver at closeout (minimum):
- Final results deck (PDF) with baseline vs POC metrics.
- Stress test report (CSV + summary).
- Runbook + incident playbook (raw text).
- Cost projection (spreadsheet).
- Decision log & risk register (this doc).

Next immediate steps (owners & due dates):
- Devon: complete KMS test integration and confirm encryption flow (due 2025-02-13).
- Aisha: share temporary API key and post initial 100-query run results (due 2025-02-11).
- Marco: prepare eval harness for NDCG measurement and seed prompts (due 2025-02-16).
- Riley: add canary config to Console with rollback thresholds (due 2025-02-18).

Notes to self / rough ideas (working):
- Consider adding a small JS snippet for client-side token estimation to reduce token surprises.
- Explore pre-warming route for morning peak to keep KV hot.
- Draft a one-pager for Acme execs that focuses on unit economics and projected savings vs cloud-managed endpoints.

End of doc.
